transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-05
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 41 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Trevor Singh (Redwood SE), Lina Park (CTO, MarlinWorks), Mateo Ruiz (Head of ML), Samir Patel (Infra Lead), Jules (PM)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on time-to-first-token (TTFT) for MarlinWorks' API use case, tradeoffs between Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, security/compliance needs, and next steps to run a lightweight latency benchmark. Team requested credits and security docs.

Topics:
- TTFT and onboarding playbook (PLG/self-serve)
- Hosted sandbox vs Dedicated pilot sizing
- VPC/private deployment constraints and KMS questions
- Cost/latency tradeoffs and fallback policies
- Action items: credits, benchmark, security docs, follow-up deep dive

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone — thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick round-robin?
[00:10] Lina Park: Hey, Lina here, CTO at MarlinWorks. We're building an in-app search and smart summarization for enterprise customers, high privacy bar.
[00:18] Mateo Ruiz: Mateo, head of ML. We're mostly using transformers on dedicated infra today, want lower latency for short completions and embeddings at scale.
[00:24] Samir Patel: Samir, infra. We'll handle networking and security evaluation.
[00:28] Trevor Singh: Trevor, Redwood SE — I'll cover the technical bits and benchmarking.
[00:33] Maya Chen: Great. Goal for today: understand your TTFT needs, whether self-serve hosted covers the first phase, or if you need a Dedicated or Private path. Also to line up a quick benchmark and get you some credits.
[00:45] Jules: Quick Q from PM side — timeline for a pilot? We want a beta in 6 weeks ideally.
[00:51] Maya Chen: That sounds doable. Typical path: self-serve Redwood API + credits to test TTFT, then if you need strict data residency or private connectivity we scope Dedicated or Private.
[01:05] Mateo Ruiz: Two core requirements: 95th percentile latency under 300ms for embeddings, and per-request privacy — no logs persisted outside our control.
[01:15] Samir Patel: Also SSO and audit logs for compliance, we have SOC2 plus some EU data residency asks.
[01:23] Trevor Singh: Okay, good anchors. For latency — quick clarifier, is the 300ms target cold-start or steady-state?
[01:30] Mateo Ruiz: Steady-state. We can tolerate a bit higher on cold but steady stream should be snappy.
[01:36] Maya Chen: Note: our hosted API typically shows ~60-200ms token latency on common short-models; embeddings vary depending on model and quantization. We'll share model-specific perf tables.
[01:48] Lina Park: And cost — we care about cost per embed at scale. If Hosted costs too much we might look at Dedicated with reserved capacity.
[01:56] Trevor Singh: Right — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and lower unit costs at volume; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives isolation but has more ops/setup time. We can run a cost projection once we have your qps and token distribution.
[02:12] Maya Chen: Do you have a rough QPS or calls per second expectation?
[02:16] Mateo Ruiz: We'll be around 50 qps bursts, average maybe 8 qps, peak 120 qps during syncs. Embeds are the heavy part.
[02:26] Trevor Singh: That's helpful. For a pilot (time-to-first-token) we typically give ~10k free credits — enough for a couple thousand embedding calls. We'll spin up a hosted sandbox so you can run your sample payloads quickly.
[02:38] Samir Patel: On network connectivity — do you support PrivateLink or VPC peering? We prefer not to traverse public internet for prod.
[02:46] Trevor Singh: For Redwood Private we do VPC peering and private connectivity. For Hosted we provide HTTPS endpoints; there's also an option for egress IP allowlists and customer-managed encryption keys via KMS for some enterprise tiers.
[02:58] Lina Park: KMS — important. Our legal says keys must be customer-controlled.
[03:04] Maya Chen: We'll include KMS/HSM integration options in the security pack; absolute requirement cases usually lead customers toward Private or a Dedicated with bring-your-own-key.
[03:14] Jules: Any friction to try hosted first for the quickstart? We want to evaluate TTFT before committing to infra changes.
[03:20] Trevor Singh: Hosted is the fastest route to TTFT. No infra changes on your side; you sign up, we provision credits and a sandbox, you run your prompt set. If latency or isolation isn't enough, we shift to Dedicated pilot.
[03:33] Mateo Ruiz: Sounds good, but how often do you see degradation in hosted — like noisy neighbors?
[03:39] Trevor Singh: We have workload-aware batching and autoscaling, and smart routing by policy. But yes, a hosted multitenant environment can see variability — that's where fallback policies and reserved Dedicated capacity come in. We'll show some traces in the demo.
[03:53] Lina Park: For the pilot, can you replicate our payloads including doc-store lookups? We need real-ish tests to validate caching and KV behavior.
[04:02] Trevor Singh: Yes — please share a representative prompt set and sample docs; we can run them through our hosted sandbox and measure end-to-end latency including any prefix caching effects.
[04:12] Mateo Ruiz: We'll share a 200 prompt sample with varying context sizes.
[04:17] Samir Patel: Security docs — can you send SOC2 and encryption-at-rest details? Also, network architecture diagram showing where logs might go.
[04:26] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Action item: I'll send the security pack and a short compliance FAQ.
[04:32] Jules: Any upfront engineering on our side for the sandbox?
[04:35] Trevor Singh: Minimal. We'll give API keys and a Postman/SDK snippet. For embeddings, a single POST. For streaming completion a websocket/stream. We also supply a small SDK sample to batch calls efficiently.
[04:46] Lina Park: On batching — we saw Redwood Optimize suggestions in your docs, are those automatic?
[04:50] Maya Chen: Some suggestions are automated: intelligent batching and prefix caching can be toggled. Optimize also gives recommended quantization and batching params based on your workload.
[04:58] Mateo Ruiz: Do you support our model of choice? We're currently evaluating an open model v1.2 family that you may not have pre-optimized.
[05:06] Trevor Singh: We maintain a model catalog; if it's not present, we can onboard it — there's a short model-onboarding checklist. Performance varies; if needed we'll compile optimized kernels and quantization profiles for Dedicated.
[05:20] Samir Patel: For Dedicated, how long does provisioning take?
[05:24] Trevor Singh: Dedicated can be weeks to stand up depending on region and capacity; typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for common configs. Private on-prem longer.
[05:33] Lina Park: Okay. Back to TTFT: what are immediate next steps to get the 6-week beta timeline?
[05:39] Maya Chen: Step 1: Provision credits and sandbox this week. Step 2: Run the benchmark with your sample prompts (we'll help run). Step 3: Review results and decide Dedicated scope.
[05:50] Mateo Ruiz: If the hosted sandbox shows embedding 95th pct <300ms with our payloads, we can probably go with hosted for beta and revisit later.
[05:58] Trevor Singh: Makes sense. We'll instrument the benchmark to capture p50/p95/p99, token counts, and jitter. Also capture cost per embed estimate.
[06:07] Maya Chen: Any legal procurement concerns we should prep for?
[06:10] Samir Patel: Standard contract requires encryption keys and audit log retention. Also, data deletion policy for dev vs prod.
[06:18] Maya Chen: We'll include retention and deletion options in the security pack; many customers set dev retention short and prod audited longer.
[06:25] Jules: Competitors — are you aware of any specific comparisons MarlinWorks is doing?
[06:29] Lina Park: We're talking to Bedrock and maybe a quick PoC with OpenAI for embeddings, but cost is a big concern.
[06:36] Maya Chen: Noted. We can include side-by-side latency/cost notes for common models (embedding families) in the follow-up.
[06:43] Mateo Ruiz: One more technical: do you support KV cache warm-up or prefix caching for our LLM calls? We rely heavily on short-context reuse.
[06:51] Trevor Singh: Yes — prefix/KV caching is supported; caching can reduce per-request compute and improve p95. We'll show cache hit-rate metrics in the benchmark.
[07:00] Lina Park: Great. How do we handle encryption keys? If we bring our own KMS, where are logs stored?
[07:07] Maya Chen: With BYOK you keep the key in your KMS and Redwood requests key ops via a controlled handshake — logs remain in your cloud account depending on config; we'll detail options in the security doc.
[07:20] Samir Patel: Can you send an example network diagram for the Private option?
[07:24] Trevor Singh: Yes, we'll attach a sample VPC peering diagram and expected ports.
[07:30] Maya Chen: Ok summarizing: Redwood will provision 10k credits and hosted sandbox, send SOC2/ISO + KMS notes + network diagram, SE will run a 1hr benchmark with the sample prompts, and we schedule a technical deep dive next week to scope Dedicated if needed.
[07:50] Jules: Sounds good. Preferred days next week for deep dive?
[07:53] Lina Park: Tue or Thu afternoons PST.
[07:56] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with calendar options.
[08:00] Trevor Singh: One minor note — if you push to on-prem later, expect additional tooling changes for KV cache and kernel tuning. We'll budget for 2-3 engineer-weeks for onboarding.
[08:12] Mateo Ruiz: Noted.
[08:15] Maya Chen: Any final Qs?
[08:17] Samir Patel: Just to confirm credits timeline and who on our side will receive the sandbox invite?
[08:21] Maya Chen: I'll CC Samir and Mateo, send redemption instructions and API keys by EOD tomorrow.
[08:28] Jules: Thanks all.
[08:30] Maya Chen: Thanks — we appreciate your time. We'll send notes and next steps.

End of transcript.
